text:
kai: quick idea dump  thinking about an 'adaptive-slot' pattern where we run a tiny fast-path lane for very short requests and keep the existing coalescer for everything else. aim: keep short-request p99 low without tanking token throughput. rough sketch below.

maria: are we talking separate queue instances or just logical prioritization?

kai: separate lightweight lane process on the host separate enqueue path, small FIFO with shallow slots. requests <32 tokens get tagged and try small lane first.
tj: main worry is oscillation and starving larger batches that drive GPU efficiency. have we modeled that? :thinking_face:

kai: baseline control is probabilistic admission for mid-sized requests + a circuit breaker that floods small requests into the bulk path if GPU utilization falls under a floor. add hysteresis to avoid flip-flop.

anya: cache interaction is big. more tiny, unique prefixes => worse KV warmup. we should measure kv_miss delta per lane.

lee: our traces showed tiny requests ~35-45% of arrivals but only ~8-12% of tokens. prioritizing them cut P99 by ~50-70ms on dev hosts, throughput drop ~4-6% depending on mix.

maria: that tradeoff might be OK if tail SLAs improve. need to see 995/999 percentiles not just P99.

ops-bot: infra-check: ensure feature-flag gating on "adaptive_slot_v1" for rollout.

kai: config prototype: 
```
queues:
  tiny_lane:
    max_inflight: 48
    slot_ttl_ms: 60
    tenant_credit: 1
  bulk_coalesce:
    window_ms: 10
    max_batch_tokens: 8192
routing:
  medium_admit: "probabilistic"
  util_floor_pct: 70
  hysteresis_ms: 300
```

lee: add telemetry: per-lane enqueue_rate, lane_p99, lane_kv_miss_rate, batch_efficiency, idle_gpu_ms. surface regression alerts for model latency.

anya: suggestion: soft degrade path if slot allocation fails, attach to best-effort tiny lane queue that accepts >slot_ttl but marks request as degraded. reduces churn and retries.

tj: eviction semantics question when tiny_lane is full and a mid-size batch arrives, do we preempt tiny slots? that would reverse the whole benefit.

kai: avoid preemption by default. instead expose a throttling hint to upstream clients and do probabilistic backoff for tiny requests under high util. preemption becomes emergency-only and audited.

maria: rollout idea: canary on 5-10% of machines with synthetic mixed traffic (tiny/medium/large). compare P99/P995 and tokens/sec.

lee: cost guardrails: monitor batch efficiency and tokens_per_gpu_second. if cost_per_token increases >3% over baseline, auto-roll back.

anya: docs note: tenant_credit should be user-visible but warn about misconfigured bursty tenants. also add recommended defaults.

kai: next steps: prototype on staging runner, hook telemetry, run mixed workload experiments, collect plots. will open RFC PR with data and config knobs. pinging @maria @tj for review before canary. :thumbsup:

maria: SGTM. include a KV-warmup sim in the test harness.

tj: will review once PR is up. ping me.

ops-bot: runbook reminder: add 'adaptive_slot_v1' fallback steps and ownership to oncall.
